lines.says: Look in the cache first for a saved copy of the note.
If a copy is there, hand it back at once.

lines.code: note = db.query('SELECT body FROM notes WHERE id = $1')
lines.says: Otherwise read the note from the database.
Keep that copy in the cache for a while, so the next reader is quick.
Hand the note to the reader.

lines.code: db.query('UPDATE notes SET body = $2 WHERE id = $1')
lines.says: An editor's save changes the note in the database.
Then the cached copy is thrown away, so nobody keeps reading the old text.

system.title: Who talks to whom when a note is read and saved
system.caption: Read the numbers in order: they are the journey. The red link is where the stale copy can appear.

items.sub: one read and one save endpoint

items.label: Notes module
items.sub: reads through the cache, saves then clears it

items.label: Cache
items.sub: keeps a note for a while

journey.title: A reader opens a note
journey.why: Someone asks the service for a note by its id.

journey.title: The service looks in the cache first
journey.why: The service looks in the cache first: a fast store of copies, so most reads cost almost nothing.

journey.title: On a miss it reads the database
journey.why: With no copy it has to ask the database, the one place that is always right.

journey.title: It then fills the cache, which is where a stale copy can start
journey.why: It then keeps the answer in the cache for a while. A copy that outlives a change is how stale text starts.

journey.title: An editor saves a change
journey.why: Another person edits the note and saves it, so the database holds the new text.

journey.title: The save clears the cached copy
journey.why: The service throws away the cached copy, so the next read fetches the new text.
